MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MARCH 12, 2024

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Los Angeles County Sheriff Deputy Okamoto.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura

City Council Members Absent:  Zerunyan* (arrived at 7:29 p.m.)

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Donald Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Michael Whitehead
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Senior Planner Whitney Berry

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

None.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-H AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Written public comment was received from Brandee Kieth from South Coast Air Quality
Management District regarding its 34th Annual Clean Air Awards on Friday, April 5, 2024 at
11:30 a.m.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230516
  PRELIMINARY REVIEW OF THE COMMUNITY BENEFITS AND AMENITIES
  PROPOSED UNDER THE CITY’S BONUS LEVEL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOR
  A PROPOSED 90-UNIT APARTMENT PROJECT
  APPLICANT: RYAN ASH ON BEHALF OF VESTAR
  LOCATION: 27525 NORRIS CENTER DRIVE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the Public Hearing; 2) Receive any
  public testimony; 3) Discuss the issues; 4) Close the Public Hearing; and 5) Provide
  a preliminary determination that the proposed community amenities and benefits
  qualify for bonus level development pursuant to the City’s Bonus Level Development
  Program.

Senor Planner Berry provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  STEGURA, TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about the number of parking spaces currently on the
property and the number of parking spaces proposed. COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also
confirmed that the proposed affordable units are moderate-income units. Community
Development Director Naughton provided an update on the number of very low-income, low-
income, and moderate-income housing units that have met the City’s Regional Housing Needs
Allocation (RHNA) requirements, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER inquired about the proposed 68’ height of the building, and
how that compares to the buildings adjacent such as Old Navy.

Senior Planner Berry explained that “amenities” are typically a gym or a space for community
use, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA thanked the applicant for increasing the number of moderate-
income units and noted that those units would serve as possible workforce housing for
teachers, first responders etc., allowing them to live in the communities where they work. She
inquired if the applicant’s request for reduced outdoor space per unit could be offset by more
outdoor communal/amenity space. She also requested that the applicant consider sustainable
building practices beyond what Title 24 requires.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 12, 2024
 Applicant Ryan Ash responded that the building height will be comparable to Old Navy and
Ulta, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER. He also noted that there are
approximately 60 existing parking stalls, and the proposed project will include 85 shared public
spaces for community use.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  STEGURA, TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  CONFIRM PRELIMINARY DETERMINATION THAT THE PROPOSED
  COMMUNITY AMENITIES AND BENEFITS QUALIFY FOR BONUS LEVEL
  DEVELOPMENT PURSUANT TO THE CITY’S BONUS LEVEL
  DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM.

**ITEM TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Public comment was received from Merlin David, Executive Director of Peninsula Friends of
the Library who shared upcoming community events.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  2023 HOUSING ELEMENT AND GENERAL PLAN ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates’ 2023 General Plan and Housing Element APRs, and direct staff to submit
  both reports to OPR and HCD.

Senior Planner Berry provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN discussed the challenges the City faces regarding the
State’s housing policies and retaining local control. He also discussed low-income housing and
affordability, and the positive perspective of helping people become members of this
community including teachers, first responders etc.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA echoed COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’s comments and
commended staff for their work on the City’s Housing Element. She explained density bonuses
and noted that we are one of the first cities in the South Bay to have our Housing Element
approved.

MAYOR SCHMITZ echoed the comments of MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA and thanked the
community for the 4+ years of work on the General Plan, and congratulated staff for all their
hard work. She explained how important it is to have a certified Housing Element and what
developers can do in cities that do not have approved Housing Elements.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT, AND DIRECT STAFF TO SUBMIT BOTH
  REPORTS TO OPR AND HCD.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 12, 2024
 B.  MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW & FISCAL HEALTH REPORT

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the Mid-Year Budget Report
  and the Fiscal Health Report.

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE MID-YEAR BUDGET REPORT AND FISCAL
  HEALTH REPORT.

MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

C.  FOUNDERS PARK PROJECT - REQUEST TO AWARD PUBLIC WORKS
  CONTRACT TO KORMEX CONSTRUCTION INC.

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Award a Public Works Contract to Kormex
  Construction Inc. in the amount of $270,435 (which includes a 10% contingency), for
  the construction of Founders Park, all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney; and, 2)
  Approve a budget adjustment in Account No. 5269-430 adding $150,000, for a new
  total account budget of $300,000 in Park Facilities Fees.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public Works Director Wahba explained that staff is looking to acquire the equipment and
purchase it directly at a lower cost than what was proposed as part of the project last year, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF. He also noted staff expects the project to be
completed this summer.

Public Works Director Wahba explained that Kormex Construction worked with the City on the
Pagliano Perimeter Pathway Project at Ernie Howlett Park, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
ZERUNYAN.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) AWARD A PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT TO KORMEX CONSTRUCTION
  INC. IN THE AMOUNT OF $270,435 (WHICH INCLUDES A 10%
  CONTINGENCY), FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF FOUNDERS PARK, ALL
  TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY; AND, 2) APPROVE A
  BUDGET ADJUSTMENT IN ACCOUNT NO. 5269-430 ADDING $150,000,
  FOR A NEW TOTAL ACCOUNT BUDGET OF $300,000 IN PARK FACILITIES
  FEES.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

D.  TASK ORDER NOS. 2024-12 AND 2024-13 FOR WILLDAN ENGINEERING TO
  PREPARE: 1) PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-25 STREET
  RESURFACING PROJECT; AND 2) TO PREPARE PLANS, SPECIFICATIONS AND
  GRANT FUNDING ADMINISTRATION FOR THE HIGHWAY SAFETY
  IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM (HSIP), CYCLE 11 PROJECT

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 12, 2024
   Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Approve Task Order Numbers 2024-12
  ($81,000) and 2024-13 ($54,033) under Willdan Engineering’s Master Professional
  Services Agreement, totaling $135,033, all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE TASK ORDER NUMBERS 2024-12 ($81,000) AND 2024-13
  ($54,033) UNDER WILLDAN ENGINEERING’S MASTER PROFESSIONAL
  SERVICES AGREEMENT, TOTALING $135,033, ALL TO THE
  SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

E.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the following recommended action
  items of the Traffic & Safety Committee: 1) Install a plaque sign below each of the
  two recently-installed “No Right Turn on Red” signs on Palos Verdes Dr. North & East
  to read: “7 AM - 6 PM”; and, 2) Relocate and install a new yellow split intersection
  ahead sign on southbound Palos Verdes Dr. East, just south of Palos Verdes Dr.
  North, at the direction of the Traffic Engineering Deputy. Attachments: Staff

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Director Wahba noted that the Sheriff’s Department monitored the intersection and issued
warnings to those who did not adhere to the “No Right Turn on Red” rather than citations, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER noted that the sign would be consistent with the sign at
Crenshaw Boulevard and Palos Verdes Drive North and emphasized the importance of
enforcement.

Willdan Traffic Engineer Reggie Greene explained the state’s guidelines for the number of
pedestrians per hour to warrant a crossing guard in response to MAYOR PRO TEM
STEGURA.

Discussion ensued about some of the community’s response to the current signage, as well
as the importance of enforcement.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Written public testimony was received in opposition of the “7 AM - 6 PM” sign by Paul Moilanen,
as well as in-person testimony from Lynn Yen also in opposition of the added signage.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE RECOMMENDED ACTION ITEM OF THE TRAFFIC &
  SAFETY COMMITTEE: INSTALL A PLAQUE SIGN BELOW EACH OF THE
  TWO RECENTLY-INSTALLED “NO RIGHT TURN ON RED” SIGNS ON
  PALOS VERDES DR. NORTH & EAST TO READ: “7 AM - 6 PM”;

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 12, 2024
   MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:
  APPROVE THE RECOMMENDED ACTION ITEM OF THE TRAFFIC &
  SAFETY COMMITTEE: RELOCATE AND INSTALL A NEW YELLOW SPLIT
  INTERSECTION AHEAD SIGN ON SOUTHBOUND PALOS VERDES DR.
  EAST, JUST SOUTH OF PALOS VERDES DR. NORTH, AT THE DIRECTION
  OF THE TRAFFIC ENGINEERING DEPUTY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Davis commented on item 7A, noting that the City’s ordinance is unique, allowing
for the moderate units in the Vestar project, as well as the parking and connectivity which would
not have been the case under State law. He also noted that the intent is to protect the public’s
right to use the public parking spaces.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG) Legislative Meet and Greet along with MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA. She also
attended a funeral service for Manhattan Beach Mayor Bill Brand along with MAYOR
SCHMITZ. She also attended the Cal Cities Los Angeles Division membership meeting.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA attended the City of Rolling Hills’ Council meeting last night
to support the City’s decision to continue its membership with the SBCCOG.

MAYOR SCHMITZ noted that the Los Angeles County Sanitation Districts meeting was
adjourned in memory of Redondo Beach Mayor Bill Brand.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce
Legislative meeting this morning and announced some upcoming events for the community
including a Business Expo at Hesse Park on April 22, and a State of the Peninsula Breakfast
at Palos Verdes Golf Club in which MAYOR SCHMITZ will be speaking on May 8. She also
reported that Rancho Palos Verdes City Manager Ara Mihranian summarized the state of the
current land movement in RPV at the Chamber’s Legislative meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER requested that the City Council add a discussion about
code enforcement to the upcoming Policy Development Session. It was the consensus of the
City Council to add this item to the March 26 agenda.

MAYOR SCHMITZ attended Coffee with a Captain with Los Angeles County Sheriff Captain
Guerrero at Reverent Coffee.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 9:09 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting in memory of Kathleen Rae
Gliksman. The meeting was adjourned to Tuesday, March 26, 2024, at 12:00 p.m. for the
purpose of an Adjourned Policy Development Session Meeting.
